title: dedicated-autoscaler: fleet throughput & burst controls + utilization reporting
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Enhancement: improves Dedicated fleet autoscaler by adding throughput guarantees, burst controls and detailed utilization reporting. Backwards-compatible config additions. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Context: Customers running Dedicated fleets reported tail latency issues during short traffic spikes and limited visibility into per-fleet throughput vs configured burst budgets. This PR extends the Dedicated autoscaler to support throughput guarantees (min sustained capacity), configurable burst token-bucket controls, and export of per-fleet/utilization metrics used by the Console and cost dashboards. Motivation: give platform teams clear levers to trade cost for short-term burst capacity while maintaining throughput SLOs and improving observability. Design: 1) autoscaler: new 'throughput_guarantee' field on FleetSpec (sustained_rps and window_seconds) to ensure minimum steady-state capacity. 2) burst controls: token-bucket implementation with configurable burst_tokens and refill_rate; integrated into request admission path so bursts can be isolated per-priority. 3) utilization reporting: new metrics (fleet.sustained_capacity, fleet.burst_remaining, fleet.queue_depth, fleet.throughput_rps) emitted via pkg/metrics and exposed to Prometheus, Console routes, and billing pipeline. 4) backward compatible: old configs default to current behavior (no guaranteed throughput, burst disabled). Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4021 - [x] Unit tests for token-bucket logic - [x] Integration test validating throughput guarantees under mixed traffic - [x] Export metrics and add dashboard panels - [x] Docs and Helm values updated Implementation notes: commits introduce an AutoscalerPolicy interface extension, a TokenBucket struct used by the fleet admission controller, and a scheduled evaluator that ensures capacity allocations respect throughput_guarantee. The policy uses a conservative allocator to avoid oversubscription when multiple fleets request guarantees. Observability: added histograms for burst consumption and gauges for current allocated throughput; labels include fleet_id and priority. Backfill of historical metrics is not included in this PR. Testing: local unit/integration harness (perf-canary) run against cpu/gpu mocks; added e2e test that simulates a 30s spike and asserts queue depth and latency stay within SLO when burst configured, and scaled capacity when throughput_guarantee set. Rollout plan: feature-gated behind 'dedicated.autoscaler.v2' flag, staged canary in us-west then global. Related: builds on prior burst reporting changes (see ENG-3902) and addresses customer ticket SUP-234. Changes: see 'changed_files' and commit list. Merge: squash and merge after approvals.

notes_for_release: Added new Dedicated autoscaler config: throughput_guarantee (sustained_rps, window_seconds) and burst controls (burst_tokens, refill_rate). Metrics: fleet.sustained_capacity, fleet.burst_remaining, fleet.throughput_rps. Feature gated behind dedicated.autoscaler.v2. No breaking API changes.
manual_steps: 1) Enable feature gate 'dedicated.autoscaler.v2' in helm values. 2) Configure FleetSpec.throughput_guarantee and burst settings. 3) Observe new metrics in the Console 'Dedicated > Fleet Utilization' dashboard. 4) If unexpected scaling occurs, reduce guarantee or increase fleet size.
notes: This PR targets production stability for Dedicated customers using bursty traffic patterns. Follow-up work planned: ability to borrow burst_capacity across sibling fleets (ENG-4120) and autoscaler tuning UI in Console (PM-220).
